title: CyberWolf Advanced Security Scenarios
description: Scenario-based questions assessing risk reasoning, architecture, detection engineering and incident decision-making.

questions.prompt: A new detection produces many alerts during a pilot. Which first step best supports responsible tuning?

options.text: Disable the detection permanently
Review representative alerts, data quality, benign counterexamples and the original hypothesis
Increase severity so analysts pay attention
Suppress every alert from the busiest source

questions.explanation: Detection tuning should be evidence-led. Analysts need to validate the hypothesis, inspect event quality and identify benign patterns before adjusting logic.

questions.prompt: A workload identity has broad administrative permissions but uses only read access to one storage resource. What is the strongest risk-reduction action?

options.text: Rename the identity
Create a narrowly scoped role and verify the workload still functions
Hide the role from the console
Rotate the role name every week

questions.explanation: A least-privilege policy restricts the identity to required actions and resources. Functional validation helps avoid breaking the workload.

questions.prompt: Two log sources disagree about event order because one uses local time and the other UTC. What should the investigator do?

options.text: Discard the source with the earlier timestamp
Normalize time zones, preserve originals and document clock uncertainty
Assume both systems are synchronized
Change original log timestamps to match

questions.explanation: Preserving originals while normalizing for analysis protects evidence integrity and avoids false chronology.

questions.prompt: A user interface hides an administrative action from ordinary users, but the API does not check the caller's role. What is the primary design flaw?

options.text: Missing UI animation
Authorization is enforced only in the client
The API uses JSON
The page has too many controls

questions.explanation: The server must authorize every protected action and object. Client-side hiding is not a security boundary.

questions.prompt: A CI pipeline can publish release artifacts using a broadly privileged shared credential. Which control improvement is most appropriate?

options.text: Give the credential to every developer
Use narrowly scoped, short-lived workload identity and protected release approvals
Print the credential into build logs for traceability
Disable all audit logs

questions.explanation: Least-privilege identities, short-lived credentials and controlled release approval reduce credential exposure and constrain pipeline authority.

questions.prompt: Two findings have the same severity score. One affects a critical, externally reachable identity service; the other affects an isolated training VM. What should drive prioritization?

options.text: The order in which the scanner found them
Asset criticality, exposure, exploit context, compensating controls and remediation feasibility
The number of characters in the finding title
Always patch the oldest asset first

questions.explanation: Severity scores are inputs, not complete business risk decisions. Context and exposure help prioritize limited remediation capacity.

questions.prompt: A hunt finds no matching events, but the relevant endpoint telemetry was not collected for part of the time window. What is the strongest conclusion?

options.text: The behavior definitely did not occur
No matching activity was observed in available data; coverage is insufficient for a definitive conclusion
The endpoint is confirmed clean
The data gap proves malicious activity

questions.explanation: Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence when telemetry coverage is incomplete. The hunt report must state the gap and its effect on confidence.

questions.prompt: A proposed control reduces access risk but introduces a single point of failure for a critical service. What should the architecture review do?

options.text: Approve it because security always outweighs availability
Document the trade-off, evaluate resilience options and assign residual-risk ownership
Ignore availability requirements
Remove all access controls

questions.explanation: Security architecture balances confidentiality, integrity, availability, safety and business objectives. Trade-offs and residual risks need explicit owners and treatment.
